title: Tag BT.709 inside the filter chain
statement: BT.709 colour tags are set in the filter chain (setparams) as well as on the output, because ffmpeg 7+ leaves primaries and transfer unset after a scale filter otherwise.
evidence: Access lane encodes: -color_primaries bt709 alone left primaries and transfer unset after scale.
notes: Set today by: tools/deliver.py TAG709 (a pack default outside mp plan). | The same note: the native VP9 decoder drops WebM alpha; decode with libvpx-vp9 (tools/deliver.py --alpha-src).

title: Lower the ceiling for click-dense mixes
statement: For click-dense UI mixes or bass-heavy beds (about 60% bass), set the master ceiling to -2.5 to -3.0 dBTP, fade the first 40 ms in, and grep the render log for 'lowered' so the renderer's second AAC encode does not drop the whole track.
evidence: own renders: track lowered 0.6-2.2 dB at -1.5 to -2.5 dBTP; -3.0 delivered -14.1 to -14.2 LUFS with nothing lowered; a mix starting on a hit dropped 4-5 dB.
notes: Tools that touch it today: ears/loudness. | plan.ceilingDb and plan.fadeInMs are read by templates/_shared/audio.py but not set by default; ears only catches the result.

title: End on 0.15 s of digital silence
statement: The last 0.15 s of the master is digital zero (near-silent after a lossy decode, skipping 25 ms of codec tail); the first sample is not zero when the video opens on a hit.
evidence: Pack rule carried over from an earlier launch film.

sources.locator: 3. Mixing rules, rule 11; 5.2 House master spec

notes: Set today by: music/mixer.py render (tail_zero_s 0.15) (a pack default outside mp plan).

title: Score from evidence, fix the worst three
statement: Before showing a film, build a 2 fps 6-across contact sheet, a 12-frame strip at the fastest move, 360 px phone frames and a double loop; score hook, phone readability, motion, variety, sound sync and brand 1-10; fix the 3 worst defects and repeat until all are 8 or more.
evidence: Practitioner method from a round method article.
notes: Set today by: tools/critic_pack.sh (a pack default outside mp plan). | critic_pack builds the evidence; the 8/10 bar is a human or agent judgement, not a check.

title: Render with a complete sound library
statement: Render only with a sound library that holds every cue id in the plan; a shared library linked from an older clone lacked all 55 new sounds, and a missing id is reported, never faked.
evidence: The integration clone's symlinked library had none of the 55 new sounds until it built its own (356 sounds, QA 0 fails).
notes: templates/_shared/audio.py reports missing ids as TODO but does not fail the mix; tools/check_ids.py resolves ids against manifests, not WAV files.

title: Deliver stems that sum to the master
statement: Every mix exports master.wav plus music, sfx and vo stems that sum exactly to the pre-limiter master, and a no-music version for re-scoring or trending-audio swaps.
evidence: Pack mixer contract.
notes: Set today by: music/mixer.py render (stems=True, nomusic.wav) (a pack default outside mp plan).

title: Delivered MP4 at or under -1.0 dBTP
statement: The delivered MP4's decoded audio is at most -1.0 dBTP: limit with 4x-oversampled true-peak detection (5 ms look-ahead), then encode two AAC probes and lower the ceiling by the overshoot + 0.15 dB until both pass (up to 8 rounds).
evidence: Our renders: the HyperFrames render lowered the whole track when the AAC read over -1 dBTP (0.9-2.4 dB on one film, a flat 4.5 dB on another); the AAC encoder overshot about 3 dB on a few transients and a sample-peak limiter at -1.9 dBFS still overshot.
notes: Set today by: music/mixer.py render (AAC probes) (a pack default outside mp plan). | Resolved 21 Oct: true peak -1.0 vs -1.5 settled: the 24-bit WAV master is limited to -1.5 dBTP, the decoded delivered MP4 must read <= -1.0 dBTP (AAC adds ~0.5 dB). | Also mp.check.loudness and tools/deliver.py (pack preset tp -1.0). Settled pair with delivery.master_tp_minus1_5.

title: Encode H.264 yuv420p faststart, BT.709
statement: Deliver H.264 High yuv420p with faststart, a keyframe every 2 s (GOP warn 5 s, fail 10 s), CRF 18-23 (23 for demos) and BT.709 tags set in the filter chain.
evidence: house delivery spec; the renderer's default CRF 16 gives about 34 MB for 15 s 1080p.

sources.locator: HyperFrames > Default quality; Environment > ffmpeg 7+ colour tags

notes: Set today by: tools/deliver.py presets (a pack default outside mp plan). | ffmpeg 7+ needs setparams for bt709 after a scale filter. | Merged: The master is H.264 yuv420p with moov before mdat, bt709 tags on HD, a keyframe interval of at most 5 s (fail over 10 s), at least 0.01 bits per pixel (fail under 0.004), blockiness under 1.75 (fail at 2.5) and a 1080 px short side. [house; pack delivery defaults; pack CRF 23 demos measured 0.008-0.03 bpp and blockiness 1.3-1.9, and two templates shipped without faststart.] | x264's default 250-frame GOP is 8.3 s at 30 fps, over the 5 s house limit. For byte-identical files use x264 -threads 1; for byte-identical stills render with GPU raster disabled (GPU raster varied at 98-111 dB).

title: Upload grain at 1.5 px
statement: Grain meant to survive platform re-encoding uses at least 1.4 px grain size and 1.5x amount (the upload-safe stock: 0.030 amplitude, 1.5 px, mono), and is masked off the top 8% of luma and flat brand fields.
evidence: researched starting value: platform re-encodes are expected to smear 1 px grain; not yet measured on uploaded copies.
notes: Set today by: layers/presets/stocks.js STOCKS['upload-safe'] (a pack default outside mp plan). | Never put heavy grain on flat brand colour fields or gradients in a CRF-heavy delivery (banding and pumping).

title: Master to -14 LUFS-I
statement: The social master lands at -14 LUFS-I +-0.5 LU (warn to +-1.5), measured with BS.1770-4 gating; the pack meter and ffmpeg ebur128 agree within 0.1 LU.
evidence: House number; only one streaming service and YouTube behaviour are documented, the short-form platforms publish no spec (grade D).

sources.locator: Platform specs, Masters for every platform

notes: Set today by: music/mixer.py master (lufs -14); plan.PLATFORMS lufs (a pack default outside mp plan). | Also mp.check.loudness. Unverified claims of -13 to -10 for Reels/TikTok exist; the planned upload test (-14 vs -10 clip) has not been run. | Merged: Deliver one master for every platform at -14 LUFS integrated (±0.5), true peak -1.5 dBTP on the WAV master and at or below -1.0 dBTP decoded from the MP4 (a web hero at -16 LUFS). [house; Platform spec: only YouTube publishes normalisation (loud content turned down toward about -14); the others publish nothing, so one -14 master is the pack default.] | spec-to-loop masters use a -1.2 dBFS limiter ceiling and measured -1.20 to -2.62 dBTP: they pass the -1.0 delivered line but not always the -1.5 master line. | Merged: Master to -14 LUFS-I (+/-0.5) with true peak <= -1.5 dBTP on the WAV and <= -1.0 dBTP decoded from the delivered MP4, LRA <= 10 LU, and the last 0.15 s digital zero. [house; house loudness contract; YouTube normalises toward about -14 (grade B) and other feeds publish no spec (grade D).] | Also mp.check.loudness. References sat at -24.8 to -8.1 LUFS and many clipped: copy neither end. Web hero -16 LUFS; broadcast gets a separate -23 LUFS / -1 dBTP master (EBU R128); LinkedIn LRA <= 7 LU. Measure the delivered MP4, not the WAV.

title: Loop length avoids AAC padding
statement: Choose a loop length whose sample count is a multiple of 1024 (8 s at 48 kHz) to avoid AAC padding, give the single-loop MP4's audio a 2 ms raised-cosine fade (96 samples) at each end, and leave the two-loop file unfaded.
evidence: Measured: a 6 s loop padded 768 samples (16 ms) past the video; an 8 s loop (375 x 1024) had none; A/V lag 0 in all builds.

sources.locator: 1. The spec, From a brief; 6. Mux

notes: Set today by: skills/spec-to-loop/scripts/mux.sh (a pack default outside mp plan).

title: Let short films breathe 10-15 LU
statement: A narrative short film master uses 10-15 LU of loudness range.
evidence: Pack master table for short films.
notes: ears/loudness warns above 10 LU unless quiet regions are planned; for a short film read that warning as expected.

title: Keep short-form LRA at or under 10 LU
statement: Short-form social masters keep loudness range at or under 10 LU, measured without planned quiet regions; LinkedIn wants at most 7 LU.
evidence: House default in ears; the trailer bed warns at 13.5 LU without its planned regions because its act-1 drone sits about 16 LU under the wall by design.
notes: sound.md's master table aims tighter for short-form ads (4-8 LU) and 6-10 LU for brand films; ears enforces the 10 LU ceiling.

title: Master to house, not reference
statement: Master to -14 LUFS integrated with delivered true peak at or below -1 dBTP, whatever the references measure.
evidence: Round-4/5 references span -24.8 to -9.6 LUFS (median -15.1) and 8 of 28 peak at or above 0 dBFS; both round-6 films ship at -11 to -12.8 LUFS and one clips.
notes: Merged: Deliver at -14 LUFS integrated (+/-0.5) and <= -1.0 dBTP, whatever the references measure. [house; References run -22.5 to -6.9 LUFS; 4 of 15 round-7 and 2 of 8 round-8 films peak at or above 0 dBFS, and the 1.8M-view hero peaks at +0.5 dBFS.] | Also mp.check.loudness. | Merged: Master to -14 LUFS and <= -1 dBTP even when references sit elsewhere: round 9 ranged -22.8 to -14.6 LUFS with peaks at 0.0 and -0.1 dBFS. [house; 4 measured references: median -18.9 LUFS; the quiet pair and the loud pair cannot support a loudness-reach conclusion (4 posts at different ages).] | mp.check.loudness enforces the same target.

title: Native master per aspect, no watermarks
statement: Upload the native master for each aspect (9:16 to Shorts, Reels, TikTok and X; 16:9 to LinkedIn and YouTube long-form; cinematic films also 16:9 on X), never a download from another platform carrying its watermark.
evidence: Platform spec for the watermark rule (reposted content with other apps' watermarks is not recommended); the routing is a pack default.
notes: mp.check.size verifies each file's WxH matches its aspect tag but not which platform gets which file.

title: Master WAV at -1.5 dBTP
statement: The 24-bit WAV master's 4x-oversampled true peak is at most -1.5 dBTP (0.01 dB tolerance).
evidence: House ceiling chosen so lossy encodes keep margin under the -1.0 dBTP delivered limit.
notes: Set today by: music/mixer.py render (ceiling_db -1.5) (a pack default outside mp plan). | Resolved 21 Oct: true peak -1.0 vs -1.5 settled: the 24-bit WAV master is limited to -1.5 dBTP, the decoded delivered MP4 must read <= -1.0 dBTP (AAC adds ~0.5 dB). | Settled pair with delivery.delivered_tp_minus1: master -1.5, delivered MP4 <= -1.0. Alternative from a streaming service's published spec: -1 dBTP for lossy, -2 dBTP if the master is louder than -14 LUFS.

title: Render only aspects with a real layout
statement: A template renders only the aspects it has a real layout for; any other aspect is marked manual and skipped, never built from the other aspect's page.
evidence: A 9:16-native vlog template wrote its '16x9' file at 1080x1920 from the vertical page (16-17 Oct, line L5).
notes: Tools that touch it today: tools/tests/aspect-builds.test.mjs. Set today by: config.mjs ASPECTS (native | relayout | manual) read by tools/mp.mjs aspectsFor (a pack default outside mp plan). | The CI test covers pack templates; for user output mp.check.size is the backstop.

title: Keep PLR at 8 LU or more
statement: No clipped run (3+ samples at full scale) or decoded over 0 dBFS, and the peak-to-loudness ratio stays at 8 LU or more (under 8 warns as squashed, under 5 fails).
evidence: House default in ears.

title: ffprobe every render's size
statement: Every render's ffprobed WxH must match its aspect's size (1920x1080 for 16:9, 1080x1920 for 9:16) before it is checked or posted; a mismatched file fails and is renamed .WRONG-SIZE.mp4.
evidence: own incident: a project render wrote 1920x1080 files named 9x16 and the reverse.

sources.locator: Environment > mp render wrote 1920x1080 files named -9x16
Render findings (16-17 Oct) and fixes in mp
v0.4.0 > Fixed: every aspect renders at its own size

notes: Also check plan.aspect / W x H of any alternate-aspect plan. | Merged: Every rendered file is ffprobed and its width x height equals its aspect label (16:9 = 1920x1080, 9:16 = 1080x1920) before it is named, posted or reported. [measured; 16-17 Oct render queue: 5 of the first 6 template lines wrote a wrong-size file (4 wrote 1920x1080 named 9x16, 1 wrote 1080x1920 named 16x9); the project path built the wrong size for one aspect in 17 of 24 templates.] | tools/mp-size.mjs renames a wrong file .WRONG-SIZE.mp4; tools/tests/aspect-builds.test.mjs (100 checks) guards the template side in CI. After posting, also read the live player's videoWidth/videoHeight (memory rule; prose-only).

title: Build then render each aspect in turn
statement: Each aspect is rendered immediately after its own build; never point the renderer at a template folder after a multi-aspect build, which leaves the last aspect's page at the root.
evidence: One hand render after a two-aspect build (16 Oct) produced a 1080x1920 file named as 16:9.

sources.locator: Why mp render, not hand-run hyperframes

notes: Set today by: tools/mp.mjs cmdRender (rebuilds each aspect right before rendering it, names the file by its real WxH) (a pack default outside mp plan). | A hand-run render outside mp is still possible; mp.check.size catches the result.

title: Upload copy under 9.5 MB
statement: When an upload tool caps a file near 10 MB, make a two-pass x264 copy under 9.5 MB that keeps resolution, frame rate and the master's AAC, upload the master by hand if PSNR falls below 44 dB, and never inject a file input or chunk the upload through page scripts.
evidence: Own tests: a 16 s 1080p CG spot fitted 1.2 MB at 54.6 dB and a 15 s ad 0.6 MB at 47.7 dB; x264 two-pass beat browser H.264 by 1.0-2.5 dB at equal size.

sources.locator: Upload copies under a size cap
Encoding: ffmpeg x264, two-pass, slow, tune animation

notes: Tools that touch it today: skills/social-video/scripts/upload_copy.py. Set today by: upload_copy.py --max-mb 9.5 --min-psnr 44 (a pack default outside mp plan). | upload_copy.py exits 1 over the cap and 3 under the PSNR floor; use -tune film for camera footage.

title: Measure the delivered file, not the WAV
statement: Loudness and true peak are verified on the rendered MP4 (decoded), not only on the WAV, because the encode and the renderer's guard can change both.
evidence: Our renders: a clean -14.02 LUFS / -2.7 dBTP mix came out at -18.5 LUFS after the renderer's guard; a sample-peak limiter at -1.9 dBFS still overshot after AAC.

sources.locator: Use it (a .wav is judged as a master, anything else as delivered)
v0.4.0 > Known weak spots > Quiet renders

notes: ears judges a .wav as a master (-1.5 dBTP, digital-zero tail) and an MP4 as delivered (-1.0 dBTP, near-silent tail). | Merged: Loudness is measured by decoding the delivered MP4, not the mix WAV: -14 +/- 0.5 LUFS-I and true peak <= -1.0 dBTP, or the file does not ship. [measured; 19 Oct run of 44 template renders: 38 pass; 6 files (3 templates x 2 aspects) delivered at -17.55, -21.46 and -22.75 LUFS-I while two of those mix WAVs read -14.0 and the plan lint passed.] | ears/loudness runs the same gate. The render-queue verdict column used +/- 1 LU; the house gate (ears/manifest.json, mp check) is +/- 0.5 LU, kept here.

statement: A video that autoplays on a web page (hero.web) is mastered to -16 LUFS-I, because the page plays at the listener's volume.
evidence: Pack preset.
